title: Validated state variables for phase-transition analogies in monitor failure
description: Curated excerpts support a cautious analogy: phase-transition tools may describe abrupt monitor failure only if a validated state variable exists.
why_existing_work_does_not_solve_it: The adjacent-field theory provides a threshold mechanism, but the mapping to agent-monitor failure is not validated.
why_it_matters: Shallow analogies can mislead experiment design unless the transferred variable is measurable.
possible_research_questions: Can a measurable monitor-load variable predict abrupt false-negative transitions?
minimum_experiment_needed: Define candidate state variables and test whether monitor failure changes abruptly under controlled noise or evasion pressure.
risk_that_gap_is_fake: The analogy may be fake if no transferable state variable exists.
